cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT.

cmeAnalyses.note: One spacecraft measurement assuming some modest westward deflection of about 5 degrees and starting nearby to the source of the eruption in EUV imagery.

note: CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. Source is a filament eruption beyond the NW limb as seen in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304, and seen close to the limb in STEREO A EUVI 304. There are two lobes of this CME, each corresponding to a piece of filament that erupted. Both pieces of filamentary material can be seen erupting simultaneously in GOES SUVI 304 imagery, so both lobes are therefore considered as one CME. The filament is located at latitude N40 and spanned from approximately W90 to W130. Gradual liftoff is seen starting as early as 2025-07-05T06:23Z in GOES SUVI 304. There is a data gap in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery such that the start of the filament liftoff is not captured.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using best fit among STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The location of the source and northern deflection seen in UV imagery were taken into consideration. The right-hand side of this CME is blocked by the pylon in C3 while the left-hand side of this CME is blocked by the pylon in CCOR-1. This CME is not obstructed at all in STEREO A COR2.

note: Extremely faint CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. Source is a second filament eruption located at latitude N40 and spanning from approximately W60 to W100. Liftoff can be seen starting at about 2025-07-05T10:45Z in both SDO AIA 304 and STEREO A EUVI 304, followed by extremely faint post-eruptive brightening. Liftoff can also be seen from the NW quadrant in GOES SUVI 304, but it appears that most of the filamentary material may have fallen back to the solar surface.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using best fit between a few frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 and consideration of source location observed in UV imagery. There is a high degree of uncertainty with this measurement due to the overall faintness and irregular shape of the CME in both SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is confidence that this feature is indeed a CME, however, due to the presence of a faint flux rope feature discernable in both coronagraphs. This CME is not discernable in GOES CCOR-1 and is blocked by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3.

note: Super faint CME with a front to S best seen in the running difference imagery in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1  and very faintly in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. No clear source found in EUV imagery, however there is very slowly developing dimming centered (S50E15) just E of the southern CH, as seen in AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. This event measured with a half width less than 10 degrees.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: A faint CME with a fuzzy front dissipating soon (or father a sequence of fuzzy faint fronts following each other almost immediately). The CME is directed to the west-northwest seen in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs. Its initial front is too faint to be seen in C3, but it can faintly be seen as one of the follow-up fronts in C3. The source of this CME is a filament eruption happening behind the northwest limb as seen from STEREO A EUVI 195/304 - especially note the wide opening of field lines/restructuring of magnetic field on/behind the limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting at 2025-07-06T17:05Z, and a bit later a minor but bright post-eruptive peeking from behind the west limb in EUVI A 304. SDO AIA 304/171 and GOES SUVI 304 also possibly see this eruption - but as a loop-like filament that seems to slowly depart the limb around 17:18Z, after first starting to rise as a sizable loop some time as early as 15:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis based on the fit of the very faint front with three coronagraphs. The source is far-sided.

Post-eruptive brightening and ejecta is seen in SDO AIA 304, GOES SUVI 304, and STEREO A EUVI 304. Dimming and post-eruptive arcades can be seen in SDO AIA 193 and STEREO A EUVI 193. Another candidate source is a possible eruption from AR 4127 (S19W62) indicated by gradually opening field lines in SDO AIA 171 starting at 2025-07-07T06:00Z and by brightening at AR 4127 seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 in the frame timestamped 2025-07-07T05:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

Also observed well in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 as wide field line opening, an EUV wave, and a brief post eruptive arcade. This source eruption may have triggered simultaneous fronts in other directions, observed as CME 2025-07-08T04:36Z (NE more in ecliptic) and CME 2025-07-08T04:48Z (far north).

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The outer LE is more visible in SOHO imagery, but the bright ejecta is observed well in both coronagraphs.

note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to overlap with bright CME 2025-07-08T04:24Z. The source is likely sympathetic with an eruption on or just beyond the NE limb around N22 that had an M2.4 flare visible in SDO AIA 171 which began at 2025-07-08T03:42Z, also observed well in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 as wide field line opening, an EUV wave, and a brief post eruptive arcade. A small filament ejecta near N20E70 lifts off concurrently in SDO AIA 304, and is another candidate source, although it erupts alongside the larger eruption on the limb. This CME front appears to be triggered alongside simultaneous fronts in other directions from this same eruption, observed as CME 2025-07-08T04:24Z (bright NE bulk) and CME 2025-07-08T04:48Z (far north).

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C3 only plane-of-sky due to uncertain source longitude, and lack of visibility in available STEREO A COR2 imagery likely due to overlap with bright CME 2025-07-08T04:24Z.

note: This CME is visible to the north/northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the northwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery. This event is blocked by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The measured longitude may vary slightly as the source location is likely far-sided and unknown.

note: The CME start time is actually 2025-07-09T13:25Z (4 hours earlier than the start time in DONKI). CME with a flux rope clearly seen in coronagraphs, first seen to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 starting around 2025-07-09T17:30Z. CME is also seen to the N in STEREO A COR2. CME was originally covered by a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, but LASCO eventually backfilled. A possible source for this CME is a filament eruption starting to the SW of AR 14137 beginning around 2025-07-09T15:30Z and moving eastward - faint ejecta can be seen leaving the disk in SDO AIA 304. If this candidate is the source of the CME, there is some significant deflection to the NW.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit of the faint front with three coronagraphs. There seems to be a significant northwestern deflection happening when comparing the latitude and longitude of the CME with the approximate location of the source - a filament eruption centered around (N12W15).

note: Minor faint CME with two lobes seen to the north in SOHO LASCO and in GOES CCOR-1 and to the north in STEREO A COR2 and closely following the wider, slightly slower, preceding CME: 2025-07-09T17:30Z. This CME is partially obscured by the pylon in C3. Its source has not been found, but is likely the same Active Region 4137 that produced the preceding, 2025-07-09T17:30Z CME.

In STEREO A EUVI 304, there may possibly be a rising loop from beyond the SW limb seen between the frames with timestamps 2025-07-11T07:45Z-08:15Z, followed by wider opening field lines between the frames with timestamps 2025-07-11T08:15Z-08:45Z. note: Faint CME to the NW seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and obscured by pylon in C3; not really seen in other coronagraphs. It is the second faint front (the earlier, 03Z front is even fainter and disappears really quickly in C2 imagery). Source is likely a slowly developing, messy eruption near AR 4037, centered ~(N32W23), starting as early as 2025-07-1tT00:54Z and lasting through the whole morning (at least to 5Z). The eruption location seems to move further west with time. Coronal signatures include developing faint dimming and faint post-eruptive arcades, as seen in SDO AIA 193/304, GOES SUVI 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is not seen in any other coronagraph other than SOHO LASCO C2, so only plane-of-sky measurement is possible.

note: A relatively narrow CME with a messy front visible to SSW in white light (as well as in running difference) imagery in all three coronagraphs. Seen more to the south and more faintly in STEREO A COR2. Its likely source is a filament seen erupting starting at 2025-07-12T08:45Z near the SW limb, as seen in SDO AIA imagery, centered very approximately at (S35W60). The source is seen in more detail in STEREO A EUV 304/195 imagery than in other EUV imagers: in STEREO EUVI 195 two simultaneous eruptions cam be seen - one in the AR 4134 (~S23W90), and the other in the filament located SE of this AR (~S35W45).

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT and corroborated by the location of the CME source (an eruption of filament in the SW quadrant).

note: Faint CME with fuzzy front seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery (too fuzzy and faint to be traced in C3 and GOES CCOR-1), and so far covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. It disappears from C2 imagery after several timestamps because of it's faintness. Its source could be an eruption in former Active Region 14134 (S21W95) that is now behind the west limb. The eruption is seen after 2025-07-12T15:30Z as an opening of field lines behind the limb in SDO AIA 193, GOES SUVI 284 and as bright post eruptive arcade seen on/behind the limb in SUVI 304. Eruption also likely seen on disk in STEREO A EUV imagery before the data gap in STEREO A, best seen as a brightening in Active Region 14134 starting around 2025-07-12T15:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative one-coronagraph (SOHO LASCO C2) analysis based on the location of the likely source eruption (AR 4134).

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2) and confirmed by the location of the source - the flare somewhat eastward of the location of AR 14199.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary triangulated fit using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the leading edge using triangulation between SOHO C2, C3 and STEREO A COR2A.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2) and confirmed by what we know about the likely far-sided source from coronal signatures - moving field lines in SDO AIA 171 and an ejecta from behind the NE limb in SDO AIA 304.

note: Faint loop CME to the SW in all coronagraphs. Start time can be a bit earlier: the CME is not clearly seen in the early timestamps of SOHO LASCO C2. No clear source found for it in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1).  No source has been found for this CME in available EUV imagery.

note: Narrow CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-08-26T21:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint high southern latitude CME/outflow with a fuzzy front, following the earlier (also very faint) CME: 2025-08-27T00:36Z. No source has been found in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2); not confirmed by a source as no clear source found in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on candidate source location using STEREO A COR2 frames only. Not visible in CCOR-1 due to faintness. Not captured by SOHO LASCO due to a data gap which began 2025-08-27T12:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. Not captured by SOHO LASCO due to a data gap which began 2025-08-27T12:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. Not captured by SOHO LASCO due to a data gap which began 2025-08-27T12:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. Leading edge is extremely faint in GOES CCOR-1, adding some uncertainty to the measurement. Not captured in real time by SOHO LASCO due to a data gap which began 2025-08-27T12:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of GOES CCOR-1 and a few frames of STEREO A COR2. The leading edge is extremely diffuse, adding some uncertainty to this measurement. cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft 3D measurement with SOHO LASCO C2 only due to lack of visibility in other coronagraphs, and the observed source around S12W75. Longitude could vary W70-W80. Half width less than 10 degrees.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very uncertain, five frame plane-of-sky measurement based only on GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. Not visible in CCOR-1; obstructed by pylon.

The source of this CME is possibly some minor brightening from between AR 14205 and AR 14206 best seen in SDO AIA 304 beginning as early as 2025-08-31T02:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Low confidence, best-fit measurement based on imagery from SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 as well as possible visible source.

note: CME first seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2025-08-31T12:48Z. The CME is also seen to the S in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely some field line movement from near the S limb best seen in SDO AIA 193, SDO AIA 171, and GOES SUVI 284 beginning around 2025-08-31T10:00Z, possibly related to a small prominence lifting off. note: CME faintly visible to the NNE in STEREO A COR2 and the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. Obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The potential source may be AR 14207 (N30E40), with an eruption characterized by rising loops, best seen in SDO AIA 193/335 starting at 2025-09-02T12:20Z. note: CME to the SW seen in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C3 and fully covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. Its source is a minor eruption at around S40W40 (or 50) seen in AIA 193 as ejecta and a following dimming, with post-eruptive dimming best seen starting around 2025-09-08T18:48Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very uncertain analysis based on the location of the source filament and on the fit with two coronagraphs: SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2, two frames of SOHO LASCO C3, and three frames of GOES CCOR-1 imagery. Not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to faintness of event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using a few frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. The leading edge was somewhat visible, but too diffuse to reliably track in GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement taken using frames of SOHO LASCO C2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 as a pileup of a few outflowing concentric fronts following larger CME 2025-09-06T13:25Z. cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1). Analysis indicates that this is a far-side event. It is not confirmed by the source, which was not found and is likely on the far side.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximage analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1). The source has not been found in EUV imagery and is likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1) and confirmed by the location of the likely source (former AR 14207).

note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. Post-eruptive arcade loops are faintly seen over the limb following the eruption, as well as by Solar Orbiter EUI 304 located at approx. N25E105.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C3 only plane-of-sky as the CME front is more uniform by C3 FOV, and no STEREO A COR2 is available to triangulate how far-sided this source longitude is. Longitude fits range from approx. E125 and E80.

note: Bright loop CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning 2025-09-22T21:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is rising field clearly over the far-sided NW limb, slowly starting ~18Z, more prominently visible starting 2025-09-22T20:35Z in SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and COR2A.

note: CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-09-23T00:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen beginning at approx. 2025-09-22T22:40Z from beyond the SW limb in GOES SUVI 304, and along the SW limb in STEREO A EUVI 304. Field line opening can also be seen in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. There is no GOES CCOR-1 imagery for this event due to an eclipse.

note: Faint CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. No observable source is seen in GOES SUVI or STEREO A EUVI imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 as STEREO A COR2 not available due to a data gap and no eruption source is observed. CME is less than 10 HW.

note: Thin CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This CME is not observed in STEREO A COR2, but it is a thin CME pointed almost directly at STEREO A (~W47.8 at this time) so it may be obscured by the occulting disk. The source may be a small brightening around S15W52 near AR 14217 beginning around 2025-09-23T22:52Z in GOES SUVI 171/195, with some field line movement extending over the SW limb at this time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft 3D measurement with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only due to no visibility in STEREO A COR2, using the observed source near S15W52 as the basis and finding a good fit at these parameters.

note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs. The source is obscured by an eclipse in GOES SUVI imagery, but there is minor brightening observed around 2025-09-24T04:15Z from Active Region 14217 (S16W50) in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery. However, it is also possible this event is far-sided due to the uncertainty in the observed source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Due to uncertainty in the source location, the measured parameters may vary slightly.

note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCOC2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be related to an eruption from Active Region 14217 (S16W51) starting around 2025-09-24T05:50Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 304 imagery. However, there is faint field line movement visible over the southwest limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery around this time which may also indicate a far-sided source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The measured parameters may vary slightly due to uncertainty in the source location.

note: Jet CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Seen extremely faintly in STEREO A COR2. Source is likely narrow opening field lines and an M1.0 flare seen from AR 14224 (S13W45) seen in GOES SUVI 195 starting around 2025-09-24T08:44Z. A small amount of ejecta can also be seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 at 2025-09-24T09:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using candidate source location, two frames of SOHO LASCO C2, and one frame STEREO A COR2. There is some uncertainty with this measurement due to the faintness of the leading edge and a data gap in SOHO LASCO lasting from 2025-09-24T09:24Z to 2025-09-24T12:00Z.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs. The source is an eruption observed from beyond the northeast limb starting around 2025-09-24T10:40Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 284, 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. It is currently not observed in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap starting at 2025-09-24T14:53Z. The source is likely related to an eruption from Active Region 14217 (S16W57) starting around 2025-09-24T14:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. The measured parameters may vary slightly due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this event, preventing a stereoscopic measurement from being made.

note: Extremely narrow and faint jet-like CME seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. No source has been found.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2). No source has been found for this CME in available EUV imagery.

note: Faint jet-like CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and not seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. One possible source could be AR 4217 (S17W65 at the time), marked by a minor brightening in this AR.

cmeAnalyses.note: Since the CME is not seen in STEREO A coronagraph and the source is not clear only plane-of-sky measurement is definitive.

note: Narrow fast jet-like CME with flattened front seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2. Resembles CME: 2025-09-24T14:36Z CME. Source is likely a minor narrow filament eruption seen close to the SW limb in GOES SUVI 304 and (as brightening to the W of AR 14224 (this AR at the time was located at ~S13W54 as seen from GOES SUVI)) in STEREO A EUV 304 around 2025-09-25T07:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs and confirmed by the source seen in GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUV imagery near S17W75Z. Note that GOES CCOR-1 was not producing a good fit.

note: Narrow faint jet-like CME to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the S in STEREO A COR2. No clear source has been found, however there is continuous activity near ARs 14217 and 14224 throughout 2025-09-25 in GOES SUVI imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Somewhat speculative analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1), however since the CME is very faint and no clear source has been found for it we have no certainty that the narrow faint jet front we see S in STEREO A COR2 is the same jet we see SW in two other coronagraphs.

note: Narrow and faint CME seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Leading edge is not discernable in STEREO A COR2 imagery. Source is uncertain, but may be a tiny area of brightening seen in GOES SUVI 304 at 2025-09-25T13:57Z located at N49E70.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C3 imagery.

note: Narrow CME seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. Source is uncertain; there is no clear source in available UV imagery of the disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Faint CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1; extremely faint and seen to the SE in STEREO A COR2. Source is likely very minor dimming seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting around 2025-09-25T18:25Z, spanning from S20 to S40 and from about W38 to W58 (centered at S30W48).

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using source location seen in UV imagery with some southeastward deflection, several frames of SOHO LASCO C2, one frame of SOHO LASCO C3, and one frame of STEREO A COR2. Leading edge becomes too diffuse to track a few frames into the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view.

note: Narrow jet-like CME to the ESE in all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1). The source is likely a C3.6 flare from AR 14232 (N02E76) peaking at 2025-09-27T02:40Z best seen in GOES SUVI 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit of this narrow jet with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 and in alignment with the possible source - a C class flare from AR14232. No good fit with this analysis for CCOR-1.

note: A super faint, narrow, jet-like CME seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 but not seen in C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Its source may be a narrow minor filament eruption in AR 14232 starting around 2025-09-27T03:20 as seen in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs, confirming AR 14232 as a likely source.

note: A very faint narrow jet-like CME to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1. No clear source found but there is minor activity from AR 14232 around the time of this CME as seen in GOES SUVI.

cmeAnalyses.note: Corrected analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2).
Approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2). Source is not clear but fit indicates that the culprit is likely AR 14232.

note: A faint CME to the SE in all three coronagraphs, possibly with a preceding fainter shock. Its source is the M1.1 flare from newly numbered AR 14232 (N02E74) and the associated wide fan-like filament eruption seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2025-09-27T07:16Z, clearly directed southward of the AR. There seem to be two lobes to this event (an earlier southern lobe - the one seen clearer in COR2 coronagraph - and the northern, later lobe, best seen in CCOR-1 and not seen in COR2). The associated filament is also seen erupting on/behind the E limb as seen in STEREO A EUV 304 imagery at the time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis including both the southern and the northern lobe of this CME and based on a fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2). GOES CCOR-1 coronagraph (specifically the northern lobe of this CME as seen from CCOR-1) does not fit with this analysis.

note: Extremely faint narrow jet-like CME to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2, too faint to be seen in C3 and GOES CCOR-1. No source has been found.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs.  No source has been found for this CME.

note: Faint narrow CME to the NW visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1. The source appears to be a filament eruption along the NW limb starting around 2025-09-27T15:30Z in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery.

note: Seemingly two jet like CMEs treated as one in this as they are associated with the same source and traveling at similar speeds to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a C7.6 flare and associated filament ejecta visible in GOES SUVI 131, 304, and 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint, slow CME visible to the NE as seen in SOHO LASCO C2. Not clearly visible in other coronagraphs. The source appears to be a slow filament eruption visible to the NE in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2025-09-27T18:40Z along the NE limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2.

note: Somewhat asymmetrical CME directed eastward in all 3 coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1). It has a clear follow-up front, best seen in CCOR-1. Its source is likely the impulsive M6.4 flare from AR 14232 (N03E59) seen in GOES-Secondary X-ray flux timeline (eclipsed in GOES-Primary) and with the associated significant fan-like filament/prominence eruption seen off/behind the SE limb in STEREO A EUV 304 and close to the limb in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2025-09-28T08:45Z. There is also a minor brightening and a very minor opening of field lines near the E limb in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Later analysis based on a good fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2), also fitting GOES CCOR-1. This analysis is confirmed by the location of the CME source (M class flare from AR 14232), however there seems to be some eastward deflection from the location of this Active Region, based on the fit with coronagraphs.

Very preliminary analysis based on the location of the flare, with no SOHO LASCO C3 imagery yet and with an imperfect fit with GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs. Needs to be reanalyzed once more LASCO imagery becomes available.

note: Clear secondary front to the East in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1, closely following the 2025-09-28T09:00Z CME. No source has been found.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis of this follow-up front is based solely on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.  No source has been found for this CME in available EUV imagery.

note: Narrow faint jet-like CME seen to SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, not seen in GOES CCOR-1 coronagraph.  No clear source has been found in EUV imagery for this event, but there is  a C3.0 flare from AR 4232 peaking at 2025-09-28T10:54Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate/speculative analysis based on the fit with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs and fitting a bit to the east of AR 14232 which is a possible source, so perhapse there is a deflection to the east because of a coronal hole to the west of the Active Region.

note: Narrow, jet-like CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-09-28T14:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This event is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 or GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is a C9.9 flare from Active Region 14233 (N17E54) peaking at 2025-09-28T13:31Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131 along with field line opening seen in GOES SUVI 195 and 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: Faint CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-09-28T19:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 2025-09-28T18:48Z to 2025-09-28T22:53Z. There is no clear source seen for this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement due to uncertain source location and lack of COR2A to triangulate.

note: Bright CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-09-28T20:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a C7.4 flare from AR 14232 (N03E53) which began at 2025-09-28T19:37Z, see in GOES SUVI 131. Filament ejecta is also seen in relation to the flare in GOES SUVI 304 and dimming/field line movement is seen in GOES SUVI 195. This event appears to be heavily deflected to the South.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: Faint CME to the East in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 (for a few frames around the Earth eclipse). The source is likely an M-class flare associated with Active Region 14232 (N04E47) as seen in GOES SUVI 131 (primary and secondary spacecraft).

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Partially faint CME to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source appears to be an M-class flare associated with Active Region 14232 (N01E47) based on GOES SUVI 131 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery, SOHO LASCO C3 is not as clearly seen in SOHO LASCO C3 due to control arm.

note: Faint CME to the East in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely a C-class flare from Active Region 14232 (N04E46) based on GOES SUVI 131 imagery (primary and secondary).

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. An Earth eclipse prevents the use of GOES CCOR-1 during this analysis.

note: CME seen east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs. It is likely associated with the M1.0 flare from Active Region 14232 peaking at 2025-09-29T11:25Z (N04E42). Preliminary fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2) indicates that AR 14232 is likely the source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs, SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.  This analysis is confirmed by the location of the likely CME source - M1.0 flare from AR 14232.

note: Very faint, slow CME seen to the NE in a few early frames of SOHO LASCO C2 only. Its front is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 coronagraph. No clear front in STEREO A COR2. No clear source has been found. The source of this faint CME could potentially be the M1.1 flare from AR 14236 (N12E34) peaking at 2025-09-29T11:52Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: 3D measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. Event is too faint to be tracked in SOHO LASCO C3 or GOES CCOR-1.
Because of the absence of a definitive front on STEREO A COR2, we can make only only a plane-of-sky analysis of this very faint front using a few early frames of SOHO LASCO C2 coronagraph.

note: Faint CME to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2A coronagraphs. Its source is likely the C4.3 flare from AR 14232 (N04E40) peaking at 2025-09-29T14:25Z and an associated narrow filament eruption directed/deflecting significantly southward of this AR, as is clearly seen in GOES SUVI 195/304 at 2025-09-29T14:24Z. There is also an associated brightening centered (S15E42) at the time. In STEREO A EUV 195 imagery, on/near the SE limb, an erupting narrow filament is seen deflecting very significantly towards the south around 2025-09-29T14:25-14:35Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: This analysis includes a brighter, more southern lobe and a more faint northern lobe, both of which are better seen in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs. If the source of this CME is indeed a flare and filament eruption from AR 14232, this analysis suggests a significant SE deflection from the source.

note: CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-09-29T15:12Z and also faintly seen in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 for a couple of frames. However, this CME is only measurable in SOHO LASCO C2 as the imagery in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 is grainy. This front is only visible in one good frame from SOHO LASCO C3. The front becomes un-trackable fairly quickly. There are a couple of source candidates for this CME. One is an on-disk filament eruption in the East with some southward deflection. The second candidate is a narrow jet of ejecta seen from on/beyond the SE limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen as this CME is only measurable in SOHO LASCO C2 and because the source is somewhat ambiguous.

note: Extremely faint CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-09-29T18:24Z. This event is too faint to be seen in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 or GOES CCOR-1. There is no abundantly clear source aside from some minor field line opening along the SE limb in GOES SUVI 195 beginning at approx. 2025-09-29T17:52Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement due to speculative source near the limb and lack of coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

note: Faint CME first seen to the East in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-09-30T01:48Z. This event is too faint to be seen in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 or GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event may be related to an M1.2 flare from Active Region 14232 (N05E35) peaking at 2025-09-30T00:56Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft measurement based on source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2. Event fades before exiting the filed-of-view in SOHO LASCO C2.

note: CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. Source is a large filament eruption seen near the SW limb of the Earth-facing disk, and in the SW quadrant of the STEREO-A-facing disk. The filament can be seen spanning S35W60 to S15W108 and beginning to show movement at 2025-09-30T08:36Z. An associated M2.6 flare peaking at 2025-90-30T09:40Z and a narrow jet of ejecta, both from AR 14227 (S17W58), can be seen in GOES SUVI 304. Liftoff of material and post-eruptive brightening can also be seen in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

Best fit measurement using several frames of STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. SOHO LASCO was in a downlink period which began at 2025-09-30T09:48Z such that the CME was only visible for two frames of SOHO LASCO C2 at the time of measurement.

note: CME first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-09-30T12:36Z. This front is also seen in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is most likely outflow at the back of filament eruption CME: 2025-09-30T09:24Z. Some additional eruptive activity can be seen near the W limb to the west of AR 14227 best seen in GOES SUVI 304 beginning around ~2025-09-30T12:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best-fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Very narrow, jet-like CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-09-30T13:25Z. The jet is also seen in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. There are two possible source candidates. The first is an eruption from AR 14232 (~N05E29) best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2025-09-30T10:00Z. The second and more likely candidate is some narrow ejecta from beyond the E limb best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2025-09-30T12:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen because source candidate is most likely beyond the E limb, and this jet is not seen in STEREO A COR2 to provide a triangulated measurement.

note: CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-09-30T14:48Z. CME is also seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. This CME is most likely outflow at the back of filament eruption CME: 2025-09-30T09:24Z. No additional source was seen, but measurement indicates that this CME is slightly far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best-fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

note: CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-09-30T23:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is likely beyond the West limb, as field line opening is visible beyond the limb in GOES SUVI and along the West limb in STEREO A COR2 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.
